- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; increase forecast downward by 1–2% to align with mean reversion.
- Model tends to lag in early periods (first 3–5 days of forecast) when sentiment is volatile; adjust downward by 0.5–1% for first 3 days if sentiment is mixed or negative.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days of history show strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive days of price decline), model often fails to correct; apply upward bias to offset mean reversion effect.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is near support, model underestimates support; increase forecast slightly to avoid missing bottom.
